commands.name: server
commands.usage: host [port] [-tls] [-noverify] [-name name] [-nick nick] | rename [old] [new] | del name
commands.summary: Connect to a new server, rename or delete one
commands.details: Opens a server tab and connects. With -tls the port defaults to 6697, otherwise 6667. -noverify skips the certificate check (self-signed servers). -name is its [server.<name>] (default: the host), -nick its own nick (default: [general] nick). The server is remembered like /set does, so /save keeps it for the next start. Naming a server you already have reconnects it. Twitch chat works too: /server irc.chat.twitch.tv 6697 -tls -name twitch -nick yourlogin, then /set server.twitch.password oauth:yourtoken and /connect twitch; /join #streamer (lowercase is done for you). Names, colors, badges, subs, raids, timeouts and room modes show up; WHOIS, DCC and Twitch's /ban /timeout don't exist over its IRC. A server that asks for TLS (IRCv3 STS) gets it: iSekur reconnects with TLS on the port it names, and remembers that for as long as the server says (the sts file next to the config; delete it to forget). /server rename gives a network a new name: its [server.<name>] in the config (saved at once, comments kept), its tab, its logs folder and kept history follow, no reconnect needed (the name is only yours). Without the names it asks, for the tab you're in; the settings window's name row and r do the same.

commands.name: twitch
commands.details: Opens the tab of your Twitch server (any [server.<name>] on twitch.tv; made as [server.twitch] if there's none). Already set up: asks to connect. Otherwise it says what's missing (your login and an OAuth token with chat:read and chat:edit) and asks for them, so the token never lands in your input history. They're kept like /set does: /save writes them to the config. /twitch token shows how to get a token: register an app at dev.twitch.tv/console (redirect http://localhost), open Twitch's sign-in link with its Client ID, approve, and copy access_token from the address bar. Once connected, /join streamer joins the chat of twitch.tv/streamer; /autojoin add #streamer and /save keep it.

commands.name: connect
commands.details: Connects the server of the current tab, or the [server.<name>] you give.

commands.name: servers
commands.details: The terminal: the settings window at the first server, where c connects the selected one, r renames it, x deletes it (it asks first) and n adds one; its keys edit it. The webchat: the Servers window (the server-rack button). Elsewhere it lists them.

commands.name: autoconnect
commands.summary: Connect this server when iSekur starts
commands.details: Without arguments, says whether this tab's server connects at startup. on / off change it and write it to the config at once ([server.<name>] autoconnect). Also in a server tab's right-click menu.

commands.name: reconnect
commands.details: Quits this server (with the message, else quit_message) and connects again right away; the channels are joined again. Also in the menu of a right click on a server tab.

commands.name: disconnect
commands.summary: Quit this server, keep the tabs
commands.details: Sends QUIT to the server of the current tab and does not reconnect. Its tabs stay open; /connect brings it back and rejoins the channels.

commands.name: quit
commands.summary: Quit every server and exit iSekur
commands.details: Sends QUIT everywhere and exits. Alt+Q (Option+Q on a Mac) does it too, after asking. To keep iSekur running in the background instead, use /detach or Alt+D (Option+D on a Mac).

commands.name: nick
commands.details: Changes your nick on the server of the current tab. When disconnected, it is used on the next connect. iSekur remembers it per network ([server.x] last_nick, written to the config at once), so reconnects and restarts use it; /set nick (or server.x.nick) goes back to the configured one.

commands.name: setname
commands.summary: Change your real name without reconnecting
commands.details: Sends SETNAME on servers with IRCv3 setname; others see it in WHOIS and the webchat nick list's tooltip. It lasts until you disconnect: /set realname keeps one for the next connect.

commands.name: register
commands.summary: Register your nick as an account on this server
commands.details: On servers with IRCv3 account registration (draft/account-registration), asks for a password (hidden) and registers your current nick. Some servers need an email, and some send a code to it: /verify finishes then. Once it works, sasl_user and sasl_pass are set for this server: /save logs you in with SASL from then on. Elsewhere, use /msg NickServ REGISTER.

commands.name: verify
commands.summary: Finish a /register with the emailed code
commands.details: Sends the code the server emailed after /register (IRCv3 VERIFY).

commands.name: join
commands.details: The # is added when you leave it out. Give the key for channels with +k.

commands.name: autojoin
commands.summary: Channels joined when the server connects
commands.details: Without arguments, lists this server's autojoin channels. add / del change the list, the current channel when you name none; add keeps the key you gave /join. Both are written to the config at once. snap makes every server's autojoin the channels open right now (here: only this server's) and writes it to the config at once.

commands.name: part
commands.details: Leaves the current channel, or the one you name, and closes its tab, like /close and Ctrl+W. The message, or else part_message, goes with it (not on Twitch, which has none); the server's tab notes that you left.

commands.name: msg
commands.details: Sends text to a nick or channel without opening a tab. If a tab for the target is already open the message shows there.

commands.name: query
commands.details: Opens (or switches to) a query tab with nick, and sends text if you give it.

commands.name: e2e
commands.summary: Encrypted chat with other iSekur users
commands.details: Asks for a password (typed hidden; an empty line cancels) and invites nick. They get a notice and accept with /e2e yournick and the same password. If the passwords match, both sides see "Encrypted chat is on" and the query is AES-256-GCM encrypted from then on; if not, both are told and nothing is encrypted. Keys live in memory only: after a restart, start again. /e2e off ends it, /e2e alone lists sessions. Other clients see +iSE lines. /e2e #channel asks for a password and encrypts what you say there; whoever typed the same password reads it (lines with 🔒), the rest see +iSE noise. No check: a wrong password just can't open the others' lines. Anyone with the password reads it all; to drop someone, change it. Also in the channel tab's right click menu. For an autojoin channel the key (not the password) is saved in the config as e2e_keys, so a restart doesn't ask; anyone who reads the file can read the channel.

commands.name: me
commands.details: Shows as "* yournick action" in the channel or query.

commands.name: notice
commands.details: Notices never trigger automatic replies, which is why bots use them.

commands.name: topic
commands.summary: Show or set the channel topic
commands.details: Without text, shows the topic. With text, sets it (channels with +t need ops). A double click on the topic bar opens it in a box to edit, in the terminal and the webchat, when you may change it.

commands.name: quiet
commands.summary: Hide joins, parts, quits and nick changes in this tab
commands.details: Toggles for the current tab only. Hidden lines are still logged and come back with /quiet off. Your own joins and parts stay visible.

commands.name: mute
commands.summary: Mute hilights and alerts from this tab
commands.details: Toggles for the current tab and saves it in the network's mute setting right away. Your nick and hilight_words stop highlighting, ringing and being copied to window 1; messages still show and light up the tab. Muted tabs show 🔇. Also in the channel tab's right-click menu.

commands.name: reply
commands.summary: Reply to someone's last message here
commands.details: Sends text as an IRCv3 reply to nick's newest message in this tab: clients that know replies show it under that message, and iSekur shows it as "↪ nick: “what they said”" before your text. A reply to one of your messages hilights. On servers without message tags (or in an /e2e tab) it goes as "nick: text".

commands.name: react
commands.summary: React to the last message here
commands.details: Sends an IRCv3 reaction to the newest message in this tab (or nick's newest). Reactions show as a line: "bob reacted 👍 to your message “…”". Needs message tags on the server.

commands.name: redact
commands.details: On servers with IRCv3 message redaction, deletes your newest message in this tab for everyone: it shows as [message deleted]. Ops deleting others' messages show the same way.

commands.name: notify
commands.summary: Be told when a nick comes online or goes
commands.details: Watches nicks on this tab's network: "bob is online" in the server tab (a hilight, so it rings and goes to window 1) and "bob went offline". It uses MONITOR, or ISON once a minute on servers without it. Alone it lists them, online first. add / del write the network's notify setting at once.

commands.name: statusbar
commands.summary: Show uptime, CPU, memory, load or battery in the status bar
commands.details: Right of the status bar (under the nick list): up = how long iSekur has run, cpu = this machine's CPU use, mem = memory free/total, load = load average (1, 5, 15 min), bat = battery as 3 bars (green, yellow, orange, red below 15%) and its %, only on machines that have one. An item alone toggles it, /statusbar alone lists them. Kept until restart; /save writes it to status_info in the config. cpu and mem turn yellow, orange and red as they pass cpu_levels (default 50 75 90) and mem_levels (memory in use, default 70 85 95): /set cpu_levels 60 80 95. The theme sets the colors: status_info, status_ok, status_warn, status_high, status_crit and status_bat. What doesn't fit is left out from the end.

commands.name: ctcp
commands.details: PING shows the round trip time when the reply arrives.

commands.name: raw
commands.details: Sends the line to the server exactly as typed. Unknown commands do this too.

commands.name: op
commands.details: In the channel's tab; several nicks at once.

commands.name: deop
commands.details: In the channel's tab.

commands.name: halfop
commands.details: In the channel's tab, on servers with halfops.

commands.name: dehalfop
commands.details: In the channel's tab.

commands.name: voice
commands.details: In the channel's tab.

commands.name: devoice
commands.details: In the channel's tab.

commands.name: ban
commands.details: In the channel's tab. A bare nick bans nick!*@*; /kickban finds the host. /ban alone lists the bans.

commands.name: unban
commands.details: In the channel's tab; the mask as /ban lists it.

commands.name: massop
commands.details: Gives +o to everyone who isn't an op yet, several per MODE line (as many as the server's MODES allows). Needs ops.

commands.name: massdeop
commands.details: Takes +o from every op but you. Needs ops.

commands.name: massvoice
commands.details: Gives +v to everyone below halfop who doesn't have it. Handy with /lockdown: the regulars can keep talking while the channel is moderated.

commands.name: massdevoice
commands.details: Takes +v from everyone but you.

commands.name: masskick
commands.summary: Kick everyone who isn't an op or halfop
commands.details: Asks first: without -yes it only says how many users it would kick. Ops, halfops and you stay. Kicks go through flood control, so a big channel takes a while.

commands.name: lockdown
commands.details: Moderated (only voiced and ops talk), no outside messages, topic lock, secret, invite only. Use it during a flood or raid; /unlock lifts it.
examples: /lockdown then /massvoice to let the regulars talk

commands.name: unlock
commands.details: Removes moderated, secret and invite only. +n and +t stay.

commands.name: kickban
commands.summary: Ban *!*@host and kick, in one go
commands.details: Bans the user's host (so a new nick doesn't get them back in) and kicks them. If the host isn't known yet iSekur asks the server for it first.

commands.name: tempban
commands.summary: Kick + ban, unbanned after some minutes
commands.details: Like /kickban, then lifts the ban after the given minutes (1 to 10080). The unban is sent by iSekur, so it has to be running then. /chanstats lists the pending ones.

commands.name: chanstats
commands.summary: Users, ops, voices, topic and modes
commands.details: Counts the nicklist (ops, halfops, voiced, regular, away) and shows the modes, the topic, the topic rotation and pending temp bans. Nothing is sent to the server.

commands.name: topicrotate
commands.summary: Change the topic on a timer
commands.details: Sets the topics in turn, one every N minutes (1 to 1440), starting right away. Separate them with |. Without arguments shows what's rotating; off stops it. It runs while iSekur runs and is not saved.
examples: /topicrotate 60 Welcome! | Rules: be nice | Meeting Friday 18:00 UTC

commands.name: win
commands.details: Same as Alt+1..9 / Alt+0, but works for tabs past 10.

commands.name: move
commands.summary: Move this tab to place N among its server's tabs (a server tab: among the servers)
commands.details: 1 is right after the server tab. In a server tab it moves the server, with all its tabs. Dragging a tab onto another of its server (a server tab onto another server's), here or in the webchat, does the same. The order is kept: channels in the server's autojoin list, servers in [general] server_order.

commands.name: close
commands.details: Parts the channel first, like /part (with part_message). On a server tab it disconnects and closes all of the server's tabs.

commands.name: split
commands.details: Opens a second pane with tab N or the tab named so (this server's first), or the next tab when none is given. side puts them side by side, stack one over the other; without either it goes by the window's width. /split side or /split stack while split just changes the layout. Each channel pane has its own nicklist (hidden when its pane gets too narrow; F2 hides them all). Typing and the topic follow the focused pane: F6 or Alt+O switches (the [keys] action is other_pane), and so does a click in the other pane or picking its tab. Changing tabs changes the focused pane only. In the webchat it works the same, per browser. Alone, while split, it says what's in the other pane.

commands.name: unsplit
commands.summary: Back to one tab at a time
commands.details: Closes the second pane from /split; the focused tab stays on screen. Closing the tab that's in the other pane does it too.

commands.name: fold
commands.summary: Hide or show a server's channels in the tab bar
commands.details: The server's tab shows +N for them, colored like their news; Ctrl+N/P, Ctrl+A and /win still go to them. The same as a click on the ▾ next to the network's name in the webchat, and in a server tab's right click menu.

commands.name: clear
commands.details: Only clears what is on screen; logs are untouched.

commands.name: grep
commands.details: Shows the lines of the current tab that contain text (nick or message, case insensitive), the last 50 at most. -all searches every tab.

commands.name: theme
commands.summary: Show or switch the color theme
commands.details: Alone: a picker in the terminal and the webchat; type to filter, Up/Down previews live (both), Enter keeps (as /set theme, so /save writes it), Esc goes back. Themes are files in themes/*.theme (also ~/.config/isekur/themes/); /set theme_dir ~/mythemes looks in your own folder first, the shipped ones still found after it. The switch is live; /set theme name + /save keeps it.

commands.name: set
commands.summary: The settings window, or show or change one setting
commands.details: Alone it opens the settings window: All, then Global ([general], by topic), each network with its own topics (open the one you pick), then Web. A network lists its own keys and every Global one it can override: "inherits" shows Global's value, "overrides Global" its own (d gives Global's back), and the Global key names the networks overriding it. / searches, Up/Down moves, Tab or Left/Right goes between categories and keys, e or Enter edits, Space switches on/off (and steps through the themes, applied at once), d or Del puts the default back, s or Ctrl+S saves, q or Esc closes; the mouse works too. The webchat's ⚙ is the same, with switches and a theme list. With a key it shows it; with a value it changes it right away. The section defaults to [general]. While typing the key, matching keys are listed and Tab completes them. /set key "" empties it, which means its default again.

commands.name: reload
commands.details: Applies an edited config without restarting: theme, keys, mouse, colors, bell, logging and the rest right away; server settings on the next /connect; [web] after /web restart. Servers added to the file are opened (and connected when autoconnect is on); removed ones stay until you close their tab. /set changes not yet saved stay on top.

commands.name: save
commands.summary: Write changed settings to the config file
commands.details: Saves what /set, /server, /autojoin and /ignore changed. Comments in the file are kept.

commands.name: hilight
commands.summary: Words highlighted besides your nick on this network
commands.details: Without arguments, lists them. Each network has its own list (hilight_words in its [server.name] section). Matching ignores case and takes whole words; * matches anything (isekur*). /save keeps the list.

commands.name: ignore
commands.summary: Ignore a nick or mask on this network, or list its ignores
commands.details: Each network has its own list (ignore in its [server.name] section): the same nick elsewhere is often someone else. A bare nick becomes nick!*@*. Ignored users' messages, notices, invites and CTCPs are dropped. /save keeps the list.

commands.name: unignore
commands.details: On this network. Use the mask exactly as /ignore lists it.

commands.name: exec
commands.details: The output shows up in the cmd tab as it comes, without blocking the chat. With -o it is said in the tab you typed it in once the command ends, unless it is longer than paste_confirm lines (-y sends it anyway). Commands are killed after exec_timeout seconds (default 30) or 1000 lines. /exec alone lists the running ones. Off in the webchat unless /set exec_web on, since it runs commands on this machine.

commands.name: dcc
commands.usage: [list] | get [number|nick] | send nick file | close number|nick
commands.details: A file someone sends you is only offered: nothing is downloaded until you /dcc get it (the newest offer, the one with that number, or the newest from that nick). It goes into dcc_dir (default ~/Downloads, on the machine iSekur runs on) without overwriting anything; a smaller file there with the same name is taken as a broken download and resumed. /dcc send offers a file (a name alone is looked for in dcc_dir; from the webchat only those) and waits 5 minutes for them to take it. Behind a router set dcc_ip to your public address and forward dcc_ports (e.g. 5000-5010) to this machine. Transfers run in the background with their progress in the status bar and the webchat. /dcc close refuses an offer, cancels a transfer or takes a finished one off the list. With dcc_web on, the webchat's Files window downloads what's in dcc_dir, like a seedbox. dcc = off (/set dcc off, every network) drops offers and turns off /dcc get and send. Passive DCC is not supported yet.

commands.name: shell
commands.summary: Open a real terminal in a tab
commands.details: Asks for this machine's login and password first (the user iSekur runs as, checked by the system through PAM; pam_service sets the service, default login; three wrong ones lock it for a minute), then runs $SHELL as a login shell on a pty: vim, top, ssh, Ctrl+C all work. Every key goes to it except Alt+Left/Right and Alt+1-9 (other tabs); the mouse wheel scrolls back. exit ends it, Ctrl+W then closes the tab. Terminal only: never from the webchat.

commands.name: attach
commands.summary: Another machine's iSekur in a tab, over ssh
commands.details: Runs ssh -t host there and isekur --attach on it (through a login shell, so its PATH is the usual one) in a tab like /shell's: the remote iSekur, live, inside this one. host is a name, user@host or a Host from ~/.ssh/config (ports and keys go there). ssh asks for its own password or uses your keys; no system login is asked first. Every key goes to the remote except Alt+Left/Right and Alt+1-9, so Alt+D or /detach typed there detaches it and leaves it running; the tab then says so, and /attach host again reconnects. If nothing runs there, a new iSekur starts. Several iSekurs on one machine each run with their own config (isekur -c work.conf); config picks one (isekur -c config --attach there) and names the tab host:work; ssh host isekur --list shows which run there. The mouse isn't passed on. Terminal only: never from the webchat.

commands.name: lock
commands.summary: Lock the session (terminal and webchat) with a password
commands.details: /lock locks now: the terminal and every webchat show only a password box, and the webchat gets nothing of the session until it's typed (in either one). The first time it asks for a password (twice) and keeps it: from then on iSekur also locks at startup and on every --attach. /lock on sets or changes it (the current one first) without locking; /lock off asks for it and turns locking off. lock_idle = N locks after N minutes without typing (0, the default: never). Forgot it? Stop iSekur, set lock = off in the config and start it again. Three wrong tries wait a minute. The config and logs are not encrypted by it.

commands.name: web
commands.details: The webchat mirrors this session in a browser. It needs [web] user and password_hash (isekur --hash-password prints one). /web restart picks up changed [web] settings.

commands.name: detach
commands.summary: Leave iSekur running in the background
commands.details: Gives the terminal back; iSekur stays connected, in the channels, logging. isekur --attach (or just isekur) brings it back, from any terminal or SSH session. Alt+D (Option+D on a Mac) and Ctrl+Z do the same. Closing the terminal or losing SSH detaches too, instead of quitting.

commands.name: typing
commands.details: Other people's messages, actions and notices appear letter by letter with a cursor, about 30 a second (a long line still takes at most 2s), in the terminal and the webchat. Alone it toggles. Kept until restart; /save writes typing_effect to the config. Quiet mode comes on with it in every channel (joins and parts would be noise between typed lines) and goes off again with /typing off, except where you turned it on yourself.

commands.name: about
commands.details: Opens the *about tab: the version, the author, where to get iSekur, its sponsored network irc.sekurnet.org and the support channel #iSekur there. The webchat shows it in a dialog (the i button, bottom left).

commands.name: help
commands.details: Without arguments lists every command. With a command name shows details and examples. Tab completes command names here and after "/". New here? /guide walks you through the first steps.

commands.name: guide
commands.summary: The first steps guide, page by page
commands.details: Opens the *guide tab: the first steps (your nick, a server, channels, Twitch, keys, settings, the webchat, safety) on pages you turn with Left/Right (empty input line), a click on Prev/Next, or /guide next and /guide prev; q or Esc (empty input line) or Ctrl+W closes it. /guide 3 jumps to page 3. It opens by itself at startup while show_guide is on: the "Don't show this at startup" box on each page (or /guide off) turns that off, /guide on back on.

commands.name: whois
commands.details: Unknown commands are sent to the server as typed, so everything your server supports works.

commands.name: away
commands.details: With a message marks you away, without one clears it. A manual /away turns off auto-away until you come back. auto_away and away_announce (say it in your channels, off by default) can be set per network in its [server.name] section.

commands.name: mode
commands.details: In a channel's tab the channel is the target when you start with + or -, and /mode alone shows its modes.

commands.name: kick
commands.details: In a channel's tab the channel can be left out. /kickban kicks and bans in one go.

commands.name: invite
commands.summary: Invite a user to a channel
commands.details: In a channel's tab the channel can be left out.

commands.name: list
commands.details: The server's answer opens in this server's *channels tab as a table, busiest first (up to 1900 rows; a new /list replaces it). The pattern is sent as typed: *word* filters by name; many servers also take >N (more than N users). /list sort name|users (or a click on the Channel or Users header) sorts it again, a second time reverses it; double click a channel to join it.

commands.name: oper
commands.summary: Log in as an IRC operator
commands.details: Without the password you are asked for it, hidden and kept out of the input history. While you are +o or +s, server notices ("*** ...") and WALLOPS go to a *snotices tab, and the nick menu gets Kill and G-line.

commands.name: kill
commands.summary: Disconnect a user from the network
commands.details: The user sees "Killed (yournick (reason))" and may reconnect; /gline keeps them out.

commands.name: wallops
commands.summary: Message every user with +w (and the opers)
commands.details: /globops and /locops (opers only, network or this server) work the same way.

commands.name: gline
commands.summary: Ban a user@host from the whole network
commands.details: /kline (this server), /zline (an IP, before the connection registers) and /shun (connected but silenced) take the same arguments; /ungline, /unkline, /unzline and /unshun lift them. Durations: 0 (permanent), 3600, 30m, 1d, 1w. Without arguments lists the active lines.

commands.name: sajoin
commands.summary: Force a user into (or /sapart out of) a channel
commands.details: /sanick nick newnick and /samode #channel modes work the same way, ignoring channel rules.

commands.name: chghost
commands.summary: Change a user's host (/chgident: the ident)
commands.details: /sethost host changes your own.

commands.name: rehash
commands.details: /die and /restart stop or restart the server. Server linking: /squit server reason, and /quote CONNECT server (iSekur's own /connect reconnects you).

guide.title: Welcome to iSekur
html: iSekur is a colorful IRC client for the terminal, with many servers at once and a
built-in webchat that mirrors your session in a browser. This guide takes ~5 minutes.
▸ How the screen works
Top the topic bar, then the tabs: one per server, channel and private chat
Middle the chat, and the nick list on the right in channels
Bottom the status bar and the input line: type text to talk, /commands to act
▸ Turning pages
← → with the input line empty, or click ◀ Prev and Next ▶ below
/guide 4 jumps to a page, q , Esc or Ctrl+W closes it, /guide brings it back
TIP Text in pink italics is yours to replace, e.g. /nick yournick.

guide.title: Who you are
html: Before connecting, pick the name people will see. These go in [general], for every server:
/set nick yournick your nickname
/set altnick yournick_ used if the first one is taken
/set realname Your Name shown in /whois
/save write them to the config file
▸ Saved or not?
/set changes apply right away but only for this run. /save keeps them for the
next start. Forgot? The settings window marks unsaved keys, and /save any time.
TIP Already connected? /nick newnick changes it now, and iSekur remembers it.

guide.title: Your first server
html: One command connects, opens a tab for the server and remembers it:
/server irc.SekurNet.org 6697 -tls -name sekurnet
/save so it connects by itself next time
/join #iSekur say hi: iSekur's home, with help, news and feedback
▸ The pieces
6697 -tls an encrypted connection (use it whenever the network offers it)
-name sekurnet a short name: its settings live in [server.sekurnet]
-nick other a different nick on this network only
▸ Registered nick? Log in with SASL
/set server.sekurnet.sasl_user yournick
/set server.sekurnet.sasl_pass secret then /save and /connect
/disconnect leaves a server (tabs stay), /connect comes back, /quit exits iSekur.
/servers manages them: c connects, x deletes, n adds one.
Right-click a server tab: Connect at startup or not, Delete server.
NOTE irc.SekurNet.org is iSekur's own network: any other works the same way.

guide.title: Channels and talking
html: ▸ Channels
/join #channel opens a tab and joins (or /list to browse, double click to join)
/part leaves the channel and closes its tab (so do /close and Ctrl+W )
/topic text sets the topic (or double click the topic bar)
▸ Talking
Just type and press Enter . /me waves is an action, /msg nick text a private message.
/query nick opens a private tab. Tab completes nicks, commands and settings.
▸ People
Click a nick to talk privately, right click it for a menu (whois, op, kick, ignore...).
/whois nick shows who someone is, /ignore nick hides them.
TIP While you type a command, the list under the input line shows what fits: ↑ ↓ pick, Tab fills.

guide.title: Your channels, every time
html: Each server keeps an autojoin list: the channels it joins as soon as it connects.
▸ One by one
/autojoin this server's list
/autojoin add add the channel of this tab
/autojoin add #private key a channel with a key (the one you gave /join is kept)
/autojoin del #old take one out
written to the config at once; a channel tab's right-click menu does the same
▸ The snapshot: everything at once
Joined all the channels you want? Take a picture of them:
/autojoin snap every server's autojoin = the channels open right now
/autojoin snap here the same, only for this server
It's written to the config at once: no /save needed.
TIP Rearrange your channels for a while, then /autojoin snap again to keep the new set.

guide.title: Twitch chat
html: Twitch's chat speaks IRC, so iSekur joins it like any other server, in a tab of its own:
/twitch opens the Twitch tab and asks for your login and token
/join streamer the chat of twitch.tv/streamer (# and lowercase are added)
/autojoin add + /save in that channel's tab: rejoined on every start
▸ Getting a token, once
1. dev.twitch.tv/console: register an app, OAuth Redirect URL http://localhost
2. /twitch token shows the sign-in link: your app's Client ID goes in it
3. approve, then copy what follows access_token= in the address bar
4. /twitch and paste it when it asks (it's typed hidden)
▸ What you'll see
names in their own colors, @ mods and + VIPs, ★ subs and raids, timeouts, slow mode...
CAREFUL The token is a password to your Twitch account: never paste it in a chat.

guide.title: Getting around
html: ▸ Tabs
Alt+1 .. Alt+0 go to tab 1-10 Ctrl+N Ctrl+P next / previous tab
Ctrl+A next tab with news Ctrl+X next server
Ctrl+W close this tab PgUp PgDn scroll the chat
Ctrl+G Alt+J find a tab by name (channel, query, network)
Alt+Q quit iSekur (asks first; Alt+D detaches instead)
▸ Showing and hiding
Ctrl+L or F2 the nick list Ctrl+T the topic bar F3 the mouse
▸ Two tabs at once
/split 3 tab 3 too (or /split #chan) F6 or Alt+O switch panes
/split side / stack beside or one over the other /unsplit one tab again
▸ The mouse
click tabs and the [Act: 3] numbers, wheel scrolls, drag to copy, right click a
tab for its menu (autojoin, reconnect, fold). Tab colors: news, messages, your nick.
NOTE On a Mac, Alt is Option. If Option keys type symbols, turn on "Option as Meta"
in your terminal's settings. Keys are yours to change in [keys] (/help set).

guide.title: Make it yours
html: ▸ The settings window
/set alone opens every setting by category: / searches, e edits,
Space flips on/off or steps through a list, d puts the default back, s saves, Esc closes.
Each network has Global's keys too: set one there and it overrides Global for that network only.
▸ Colors
/theme lists the themes, /theme dracula tries one live. Some to try:
dracula tokyonight catppuccin-mocha gruvbox nord github-light
The one you pick is kept: the next start opens with it, no /save needed.
mirc draws its windows like Windows 95; ayu, github-light add Mac buttons.
▸ Little extras
/typing on messages type themselves out, letter by letter
/quiet hide joins, parts and quits in this channel
/statusbar cpu on CPU, memory, load or battery in the status bar
/set timestamp %H:%M:%S seconds in the time stamps
/set timestamp_align right the time at the right edge of the chat

guide.title: Never miss a thing
html: ▸ Highlights
Lines with your nick light up, ring the bell and are copied to tab 1 (hilight_window).
/hilight add word + /save lights up other words too.
▸ Logs
After a restart every channel and query shows its last lines again (keep_history).
/set log on + /save also writes them all to disk. /grep text searches this tab.
▸ Stay online when you leave
Ctrl+Z , Alt+D or /detach gives the terminal back and keeps iSekur connected.
Later, from any terminal or SSH session: isekur --attach (or just isekur).
On another computer: /attach host shows that machine's iSekur in a tab (over ssh).
Several at once: one config each, isekur -c work.conf; isekur --list shows them,
isekur -c work.conf --attach or /attach host work.conf picks one.
Away while detached: you are marked away by yourself, and back when you type.
TIP Closing the terminal or losing SSH detaches too: nothing is lost.

guide.title: The webchat
html: The same session, live, in a browser (phones too). Set a login once:
1. in your shell: isekur --hash-password and copy what it prints
2. /set web.user me
3. /set web.password_hash the-hash then /save
4. /web start and open http://127.0.0.1:8443
▸ From another machine
/set web.bind 0.0.0.0: then it's HTTPS only (a self-signed certificate is made,
or give web.cert and web.key). /set web.autostart on starts it with iSekur.
▸ Tabs in the browser
‹ at the top of the tab list folds it to a strip, › opens it. 👥 hides the users.
/split 3 and /unsplit work there too, for that browser only.
The server-rack button lists your servers: edit, connect, delete or add one.
/set web_font sans and /set web_font_size 16: the browser's font and size.
/set web_tree_lines on: faint lines join each network to its channels.
TIP Run it on a server with isekur --daemon: always online, chat from anywhere.

guide.title: Privacy and safety
html: /lock on a password before anything shows (startup, attach, /lock)
/e2e nick end-to-end encrypted private chat with another iSekur user
/ignore nick never see them again (/save to keep it)
/dcc files sent to you wait for /dcc get: nothing downloads by itself
CAREFUL The config file holds your passwords: it is created private (only you can read
it). Don't paste it anywhere. Passwords never show in /set or the settings window.
NOTE Self-signed server? /server host 6697 -tls -noverify, only if you trust it.

guide.title: You're ready
html: ✔ Set your nick: /set nick yournick
✔ Connect: /server irc.SekurNet.org 6697 -tls -name sekurnet
✔ Join: /join #iSekur
✔ Every time: /autojoin snap
✔ Keep the rest: /save (themes and autojoin keep themselves)
▸ Where to look next
/help every command, by group
/help command details and examples (/help server, /help set)
/set every setting, explained in the config file too
/guide this guide, any time
Questions, ideas, bugs? #iSekur on irc.SekurNet.org: see you there. Have fun!

themes/<name>.theme (also ~/.config/isekur/themes/)
where themes are looked for first, e.g. ~/mythemes
webchat font: theme (its font, else mono) | mono | sans | serif
webchat text size in px
on: faint ├ └ lines join the webchat's channels to their network
e.g. %H:%M:%S (empty: the theme's, [%H:%M] in mirc)
left | right (the right edge of the chat, terminal and webchat)
lines kept in memory per tab (min 100); fewer = less memory
auto (truecolor if $COLORTERM says so) | truecolor | 256
click tabs/nicks, wheel scrolls, drag copies; F3 toggles
open the first steps guide (/guide) at startup
Flood control: lines sent at once, then one every N ms (0 = no limit).
Chat logs: channels and queries go to <log_dir>/<server>/<name>.log (private files, formatting stripped). Any of these can also be set per server.
default: "logs" next to this file, e.g. ~/irclogs
lines restored into a tab from its log (0 = off)
start a new file each day; old ones become <name>.YYYY-MM-DD.log
log off: tabs still show their last log_history lines after a restart
Copy highlights and private messages to window 1 ("what did I miss").
What you leave with (/quit and /part without text). Empty: "iSekur <version> :: colorful terminal IRC client :: <github link>". Can be set per server too.
Join a channel again right after being kicked from it (with its autojoin key). Per server too.
The iSekur banner at startup: in the theme's colors, or white and gray.
A light sweeps across it once when iSekur starts in a terminal (not with banner_mono).
Once a day, ask github.com for the latest iSekur release; a newer one shows in /about and lights the webchat's ⓘ. The request carries nothing about you.
Right of the status bar: up (iSekur's uptime), cpu (this machine's CPU %), mem (memory free/total), load (load average), bat (battery, laptops only). Or /statusbar cpu on and /save.
When cpu and mem catch the eye: "min avg max" percents (memory: % in use). At min the value turns yellow, at avg orange, at max red.
Other people's messages type themselves out, letter by letter (/typing toggles it).
Ring the terminal bell for private messages, mentions of your nick and invites (most terminals then flash, bounce the dock icon or play a sound).
/exec: shell commands are killed after this many seconds (0 = never). The webchat can't run them unless exec_web = on (anyone logged in to it could).

A password before anything shows, in the terminal and the webchat: at startup, on every attach and after /lock. /lock sets it the first time (it's stored hashed here), /lock on changes it, /lock off turns it off.
Lock by itself after this many minutes without typing (0 = never)
Ask before sending a paste longer than this many lines (0 = never ask). Servers with IRCv3 draft/multiline get a paste as one message.
Tell the others in a channel or query that you're typing (IRCv3 +typing): "bob is typing..." on their side. Theirs always shows in the status bar.

Mark yourself away when nobody is attached for 30s (--daemon with no browser open), or after auto_away_idle minutes without typing (0 = only when detached). Typing anything brings you back; a manual /away is left alone. A network can turn it on or off for itself with auto_away in its [server.name] section.
Also say it in your channels (/me is away: <message>, then /me is back) when auto-away sets or clears it. Off by default; many channels dislike it.
On join, fetch what was said since the last line you have, from servers with IRCv3 chathistory (max 500, 0 = off).
CTCP answers (at most one reply every 2s per server, against floods). VERSION says e.g. "iSekur 0.5 :: Linux 6.8.0/x86_64 :: ... :: <github link>".
DCC file transfers: off drops offers people send you and turns off /dcc get and /dcc send, on every network.
Files sent to you (DCC SEND) wait for /dcc get, then download here; the status bar shows the progress. On a VPS that's the VPS's disk.
/dcc send: the address offered (empty: the one the IRC connection uses) and the ports to listen on (empty: any). Behind a router: your public address, and forward those ports to this machine.
The webchat's Files window downloads what's in dcc_dir (a seedbox).
